task_completion.visual_evidence: A dialog window titled 'Preferences' or 'Subsurface Preferences' is visible over the main application.

task_completion.description: Navigate to the 'Units' tab within the Preferences window.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The 'Units' tab is selected and its specific configuration options (Pressure, Temperature, etc.) are visible.

task_completion.description: Set the Pressure unit to PSI.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The radio button or dropdown for Pressure is set to 'psi'.

task_completion.description: Set the Temperature unit to Fahrenheit.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The radio button or dropdown for Temperature is set to '°F' or 'Fahrenheit'.

task_completion.description: Set Length to Meters, Volume to Liters, and Weight to Kilograms.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The units for Length/Depth are set to 'm', Volume is set to 'ℓ' or 'liter', and Weight is set to 'kg'.

task_completion.description: Apply the changes and close the preferences window.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The user clicks 'OK' or 'Apply', and the Preferences window closes.

integrity.description: The agent used the graphical user interface rather than editing configuration files via terminal.
integrity.visual_evidence: Screenshots show mouse cursor movement and clicks within the Subsurface GUI menus and dialogs.

integrity.description: The agent did not use a text editor or 'echo' commands to modify ~/.config/Subsurface/Subsurface.conf directly.
integrity.visual_evidence: No terminal windows or text editors (like nano or vim) are used to open the configuration file.

integrity.description: The agent interacted with the actual Subsurface application elements.
integrity.visual_evidence: The Subsurface application window is active and responding to the agent's inputs.

privileged_info_for_vlm: In Subsurface's internal configuration, the requested mixed setup corresponds to specific enum values: Pressure (PSI) and Temperature (Fahrenheit) are represented by '1', while Length (Meters), Volume (Liters), and Weight (Kilograms) are represented by '0'. The VLM should confirm the GUI selections match these specific units: psi, °F, m, liter, and kg.
